result.title: Signals: Continuous Diagnostics of AI Agents
result.summary: AI agents can make incorrect decisions or waste resources even when their tools and infrastructure work normally. Their nondeterministic behavior makes these problems difficult to reproduce and diagnose. We developed Signals to identify such problems from agentic traces and suggest concrete remediations. We built the method around a taxonomy of 45 problem types across eight families, with definitions and evidence requirements for each type. The method distinguishes realized failures, risk exposures, and inefficiencies, groups related findings into engineering issues called Signals, and assesses their severity from the supporting evidence. Each Signal includes actions a developer can take and checks for evaluating the change. Further executions can add evidence to an existing Signal or reveal a new problem. We evaluated the method on public agent executions and achieved 91.43% F1 when matching Signals to reference issues, about 18 percentage points higher than a one-pass LLM control that used the same model and taxonomy.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Signals，一种基于 45 种问题类型（分属八类）的 AI agent 执行轨迹诊断方法，区分已实现失败、风险暴露与低效，将证据聚合为带严重度与修复建议的 Signal，并在公开执行上取得 91.43% 的匹配 F1。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按证据要求归类轨迹问题、评估严重度并给出修复检查的框架，可能为 LVR 中 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的失败归因、视觉证据筛选和推理轨迹诊断提供评价线索，但问题类型能否映射到 latent 推理状态仍需核查。
